metadata.name: [GCP BigQuery OTel] Batch job backlog not draining
metadata.description: Alerts when non-interactive BigQuery jobs (batch-priority queries and load, copy, or extract jobs) are pending in at least 90 one-minute samples and at least 95% of the published minutes in the last 2 hours, and are still pending in the last 20 minutes. One alert per project, location, and job type.

data.content:
## BigQuery batch job backlog not draining

Batch-priority work, which waits for idle capacity by design, has not been able to start for about two hours. Pipelines that depend on these jobs (ETL, loads, exports) are falling behind.

### Condition
- Per minute: `job/num_in_flight` with `state == "pending"`, excluding interactive-priority queries (a series with interactive priority but no job type label counts as an interactive query and is covered by the interactive queueing rule; other series without a job type are kept and alerted as job type `unknown`), summed per project, location, and job type.
- Published minutes: minutes with any `job/num_in_flight` sample for the project and location. A published minute without a pending sample counts as drained.
- Alert when >= 1 job is pending in >= 90 one-minute samples within the 2-hour look-back, in >= 95% of the published minutes, and in at least one minute of the last 20 minutes. About 108 minutes are published because of the ~12-minute publish delay.
- The alert recovers when no pending minute has been published for 20 minutes, or when the share of backlogged minutes falls below 95%.

### Triage
1. Open the [GCP OTel] BigQuery dashboard and check jobs in flight by state, slots allocated, and reservation utilization.
2. Pending batch queries: the reservation or on-demand pool has had no idle capacity for hours. Check the reservation saturation alert.
3. Pending load jobs: the shared load slot pool or the assigned `PIPELINE` reservation is exhausted, or load quotas are being hit.
4. Check for a single long-running job holding capacity.

### Tuning
- `backlogged_minutes >= 90`: persistence. It decides when collector gaps leave fewer than about 95 published minutes.
- `backlogged_pct >= 95.0`: share of published minutes with a backlog. It decides when the window is fully published. Lower it to alert on queues that drain more often.
- `last_backlogged_at >= NOW() - 20 minutes`: the backlog must still be visible. Keep it above the ~12-minute publish delay.
- To page on this rule, also route it by job type. Load backlogs usually matter more than batch query backlogs.

### Notes
- Data: `metrics-gcp.bigquery.otel-*` (OTel `googlecloudmonitoring` receiver). Dashboard: [GCP OTel] BigQuery.
- GCP publishes BigQuery metrics with a delay, so the look-back is longer than the condition and unpublished minutes are never treated as drained.
- The query returns at most 50 breaching rows; each returned row is one alert. Thresholds are marked `// Customize:` in the query.
